rationale:
bugs_open/219. validate_page_content's meta-commentary check is a raw case-insensitive substring scan over the WHOLE assembled page HTML, at blocker severity — and a blocker makes the action return an error, so the step fails and the page is never saved. On loancalculator.co.uk that convicted a HUMAN's documentation: three locked calculator components explain their own arithmetic in a /* ... */ comment inside their <script>, and those notes contain the string 'input_schema' because that is the name of the thing they document. The notes predate the run by five days and already ship to readers. Effect: those pages can NEVER be rebuilt — every content change fails identically, with an error blaming the model.

The mechanism was established by prediction, not argument. A voice rewrite was dispatched at all 12 pages carrying a locked tool component; exactly the 3 whose template contains the string failed, and the other 9 passed. car-finance was fired three times and failed identically each time.

THE BUG FILE'S OWN LEADING FIX CANDIDATE WAS WRONG AND THIS SUBMISSION CORRECTS IT. 219 says 'strip HTML comments before scanning'. Measured today: in all three templates the hit lies between a <script> open and its </script> close, and two of the three contain NO HTML comment at all. A comment-stripper would have shipped inert and the pages would still be blocked. What is wrong is the SCOPE of the scan, not the comment syntax — which is why this change re-scopes rather than strips.

The fix is the seam bugs_open/218 already settled for the sibling placeholder scan in this same file, in the same round, after a council REVISE that said: reuse ExtractAssertionText, do not add a second stripper. Meta-commentary patterns are prose patterns; they scan assertion text. ExtractAssertionText is a real HTML parse whose non-assertion set excludes script/style/code/pre/head/template/noscript/svg/iframe and attributes, and whose walk skips comments and doctypes. headProseBlocks re-adds <title> and the meta descriptions, which the extractor drops with the rest of <head> — without that this would be a narrowing rather than a re-scoping, and it is the exact escape 35889819c had to reopen for the placeholder scan a few hours earlier.

plan.summary: Re-scope checkMetaCommentary from a raw substring scan of the whole assembled page to the prose scope the sibling checks in this file already use (datahelpers.ExtractAssertionText + headProseBlocks). This makes a human's code comment structurally incapable of blocking a page rebuild, while keeping every pattern a blocker in visible copy — including <title> and meta descriptions. Also corrects the issue Description, which asserted a cause the check cannot know ('the model wrote about its task instead of doing it'), and a stale doc comment claiming a false positive here routes to needs_human_review rather than failing the build.

edits.rationale: The scan's scope, not its pattern list, is the defect. Reusing the claims checks' existing prose extractor puts every non-assertion context (script, style, code, pre, head, attributes, comments) out of reach in one move, so no future template comment can block a rebuild. headProseBlocks is appended so title/meta-description prose is still scanned — the same escape the placeholder scan had to reopen.

The paragraph above the pattern list claimed 'A false positive here routes to needs_human_review, not silent breakage', and that false belief is why the list's narrowness was treated as sufficient containment. Verified false at the categorise block: a blocker returns an error from the action, so the step fails and nothing is saved. Correcting it visibly rather than deleting it, so the next reader sees what was believed.

The pass half pins the live case (a JS comment inside <script>, verbatim from the live tool-car-finance-pcp-hp template) plus the HTML-comment, style, code-sample and attribute variants. The block half is the negative control — a re-scoping must not retire the rule, so each pattern family is induced in real copy, including title and meta description, and asserted to be a blocker with a location. A scan that cannot fail is not a check.

That is a legitimate product description and it matches the 'as an ai' pattern in VISIBLE ASSERTION TEXT, so it is a blocker before this change and after it: running the new checkMetaCommentary over that row's real rendered_html (12,879 bytes) still returns a blocker, value 'as an ai', location 'calBusiness schema, as an AI-builder prompt'.
